samples.name: Pebble Sneak
samples.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE portrait 4:5 full-bleed card illustration for original Scoundrel, Ash & Briar color-story revision.
Reference image: the supplied Ash & Briar concept board guides ONLY the simple painterly rendering and overall restrained taste. Do NOT inherit its monochrome backgrounds, poses or all-over color washes.
Primary request: distinct individual fantasy card art, with the visual storytelling and rich LOCAL COLOR RELATIONSHIPS of Legends of Runeterra, rendered MUCH MORE SIMPLY than realistic collectible-card art. Invent original characters and objects. Each scene has its own moment, environment, accent, material and lighting, even while sharing a deck.
STYLE: broad elegant opaque gouache paint shapes, calm areas, selective crisp edges at face/item, a little beautifully chosen detail at the focal point. No uniform tessellated chipping or triangular brush noise across every surface. Simple painted scenery, real spatial depth. Strong silhouette reads at thumbnail size. Modest amount of contextual detail that tells this card's story; allow the subject to touch and interact with its environment.
COLOR: suit color belongs mainly to the subject/material, NOT the whole picture. Combine three clearly separate color families with warm/cool contrast, neutrals and localized accents. Do NOT tint the entire painting grey, green, blue or red. Preserve colors of individual materials. Let the environment have colors different from the subject. Use the SPECIFIC color story below.
COMPOSITION: portrait 4:5, one main subject, natural asymmetry, directional lighting, central 80% safe for later cropping. Full-bleed painting with no text, numbers, suit symbols, frame, panels, swatches, logo or watermark.
Avoid: photorealism, 3D plastic, ornate over-detailed equipment, thousands of leaf/crack details, particles everywhere, photographic microtexture, repetitive faceted scuffs, busy collage, generic studio backdrop, uniform matching background, copy of any franchise character.

Subject and scene: Pebble Sneak: tiny round-headed squat living STONEKIN child, slate-grey smooth pebble body with stubby limbs and a cheeky sly squint. Crouched SIDEWAYS on a sunlit terracotta market step, pinching ONE oversized brass coin with two fingers while glancing over shoulder. A short dusty-plum cloth sash is the single distinctive costume detail. High three-quarter full-body view, head slightly off center, one broad muted TEAL cloth awning shape above casts a cool shadow across the ochre step. Palette: neutral slate-grey character, terracotta/ochre environment, teal shadow, small plum and brass accents. Warm late-afternoon sunlight picks out the face and coin. A little story of a theft, one coin only, NO crowd, stone arch or mountain background. Clean quiet uncracked stone planes and expressive eyebrows, not many tiny chips.

Face bowed toward his own palm, serene ancient half-closed eye; a broad moss-green patch crosses one shoulder. Low viewpoint from a cliff edge, huge hand lower foreground, head upper middle; ONE tiny off-white lighthouse on the distant shore establishes scale, simplified to a shape with a tiny warm light. Subject and scene: Pebble Sneak, a tiny round-bodied young STONEKIN thief. Stonekin are original living rock people with expressive angular stone faces; this one is squat and pebble-like, HUGE round head, short stubby limbs, no horns, no clothing or armor. He crouches on all fours, one palm on the floor, the other hugging ONE small smooth dark pebble, looking up sideways with a cheeky squint. HIGH THREE-QUARTER OVERHEAD VIEW showing the entire small character, a compact curled silhouette in the lower center, a long simple shadow diagonally away. One broad pale chalk-stone ground, NO doorway, castle or distant mountains. Palette pale blue-grey #C6CCD0 and slate #687483, charcoal #282D36 shadows. Soft daylight and a slightly warm cream ground for contrast. Broad smooth shapes, not cracked rock texture. Must look radically different from a standing broad-chested stone guard portrait.
